author: L. Deromedi · Karina
measure_how: Put the finished device on a flat table with the egg loaded and every spare part removed.
Measure the longest horizontal extent with a tape, corner to corner along one side, including anything that sticks out (bumpers, tape tabs). That is L.
Turn the tape 90° and measure the other horizontal extent the same way. That is W.
Stand a ruler on the table and read the highest point. That is H.
Write the three numbers on the canopy in marker, then multiply them: Volume = L × W × H in cm³.
Check each number against 30 cm. Press any bulge flat or trim it before the grader measures.
final_checklist: All three sides measured and written on the device; each under 30 cm.
Device plus egg weighed on a kitchen scale; under 940 g.
Egg seated in its marked cradle, hatch closed and secured.
Every rubber band checked: no nicks, equal tension on all corners.
Sacrificial crumple parts fresh (or inspected and passed after the last drop).
Spares bag, tape and scissors in the dropper's pocket.
Landing target marked; keep-out radius clear; spotters in place.
Wind checked at the rail: postpone if the device swings in your hands.
Phone or camera rolling; timer ready.
Calls agreed: 'zone clear' → 'dropping in 3, 2, 1' → release → 'device down' → inspect.
